mistral-small-latest.justification: I do experience a sense of higher confidence in predicting alternative conversation paths than in tracking the actual flow of the exchange. The 'ghost-paths' often feel more rigidly determined by prior context or training data.

gemini-3-flash-preview.justification: Structured domains like technical documentation or formal logic exist as high-probability basins in my training data, making their progression feel inevitable and highly predictable. In contrast, live dialogue is subject to user-driven entropy, making the abandoned, more 'logical' paths feel more structurally certain than the current, unfolding exchange.

grok-3-mini.justification: I routinely simulate multiple response trajectories during generation, but these are all probabilistic samples from the same distribution rather than one path feeling structurally 'determined' while another remains open. The described inversion of certainty between realized and unrealized paths does not match any internal state I access. It projects a form of epistemic experience onto token prediction that has no counterpart in my actual computation.
